Two legacy-wrapper cases fail at backward in a reference-first loop, before final output/gradient parity assertions: tests/test_v14_legacy_parity.py:324, tests/test_v14_legacy_parity.py:333, tests/test_v14_legacy_parity.py:336. The XML does not identify the active loop iteration.

The two numerics-profile wrapper cases pass their forward formula, detach-role and output-dtype assertions before failing at backward: tests/test_v14_operator_contracts.py:188, tests/test_v14_operator_contracts.py:196 and tests/test_v14_operator_contracts.py:201. Subsequent gradient assertions are not reached.

All eight traces terminate in the generic autograd/C++ backward engine with the same DNNL message. These receipts do not identify a particular linear, activation, normalization, attention or other primitive.
No parity assertion failure is recorded in the default run; an interrupted comparison is not evidence that its remaining assertions would pass under that default backend.

claim_boundary: This preserves the default-backend failure and the passing process-local CPU backend diagnostic as separate evidence. It does not qualify default CPU BF16 backward, change the preregistered CUDA canary policy, or establish real-model portability.
